Sources and Further Reading

These are the standard works behind the claims in this dossier. They are listed so every assertion can be traced and independently checked. They represent a range of positions on purpose — an arbiter reads all sides.

Bible — text & transmission

  • Bruce M. Metzger & Bart D. Ehrman, The Text of the New Testament.
  • Bart D. Ehrman, Misquoting Jesus; The Orthodox Corruption of Scripture; How Jesus Became God.
  • Daniel B. Wallace (ed.), Revisiting the Corruption of the New Testament.
  • Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible.
  • The Dead Sea Scrolls scholarship (Great Isaiah Scroll, 1QIsaᵃ).

Christian origins & Christology

  • Larry W. Hurtado, Lord Jesus Christ: Devotion to Jesus in Earliest Christianity.
  • Richard Bauckham, Jesus and the God of Israel.
  • Bart D. Ehrman, How Jesus Became God (counter-position).
  • J. N. D. Kelly, Early Christian Doctrines (Nicaea → Chalcedon).

Trinity — philosophy & coherence

  • Thomas McCall & Michael Rea (eds.), Philosophical and Theological Essays on the Trinity.
  • Richard Swinburne, The Christian God.
  • Brian Leftow / Peter van Inwagen / Dale Tuggy — contrasting analytic positions (defenses and critiques).

Qur'an — text & transmission

  • François Déroche, Qur'ans of the Umayyads; The One and the Many.
  • Behnam Sadeghi & Mohsen Goudarzi, "Ṣanʿāʾ 1 and the Origins of the Qurʾān" (Der Islam, 2012).
  • Asma Hilali, The Sanaa Palimpsest.
  • Keith E. Small, Textual Criticism and Qurʾān Manuscripts.
  • Nicolai Sinai, The Qur'an: A Historical-Critical Introduction.
  • Angelika Neuwirth, The Qur'an and Late Antiquity.
  • Gabriel Said Reynolds, The Qur'an and the Bible.
  • John Wansbrough, Quranic Studies; Patricia Crone & Michael Cook, Hagarism (revisionist — included for completeness; now minority).

Tahrif — Islamic theology of corruption

  • Classical: Ibn Hazm (tahrif al-nass); al-Razi & others (tahrif al-maʿna); Ibn Khaldun.
  • Modern survey: Gordon Nickel, Narratives of Tampering in the Earliest Commentaries on the Qurʾān.
  • Abdullah Saeed, "The Charge of Distortion of Jewish and Christian Scriptures" (The Muslim World).

On using debates responsibly

Public debates (Shabir Ally, James White, Jay Smith, Yasir Qadhi, Mohammed Hijab, William Lane Craig, Mike Licona, et al.) are useful as maps of arguments, not as evidence. Always trace a debate claim back to the academic literature above before weighting it.

Bibliographic detail (editions, years) should be verified against a library catalogue before citation in formal work — titles and authors here are accurate to the best of standard reference knowledge; exact imprints are not reproduced from memory to avoid false precision.
